newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada gold sector sinks, some juniors rebound.
newsitem.headline: Canada gold sector sinks, some juniors rebound.

text.p: The Toronto Stock Exchange gold group sank to a 52-week low on Monday, hit by a general malaise as well as continued jitters about the future of Bre-X Minerals Ltd and its Indonesian gold property.
But analysts said the sector is just now returning to "fair value" after a long stint at lofty levels.
The group was down 92.37 points, or nearly one percent, to 9467.17. This was up from a year-low of 9309.71 hit earlier.
"They have been inflated for some time. It's been the longest run-up, or inflated values, that we have seen ever," Barry Allan of Gordon Capital Corp said.

"So on a relative basis (to the TSE 300), yeah, the sector looks cheap. But you have to go back and look at it on an absolute basis. We are only really coming into fair value now, even after what's gone on up to Friday," Allan added.

On Wednesday and Thursday, gold shares sold off sharply after Bre-X's partner Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc cast doubt on the company's claims that it had found a massive gold deposit in Indonesia.
Some junior shares recovered part of the ground lost last week on Monday. Corriente Resources Inc shares spiked 2.55 to 15.85 in active trade.
Indochina Goldfields Ltd climbed 1.60 to 14.25 while Scorpion Minerals moved up 1.10 to 3.70.
Senior gold shares did not fare as well. But analysts said Bre-X is not the only culprit in the gold sector's fall.
An erosion in the gold price in recent weeks has spooked technical analysts who believe a breach of the US$343 per ounce level would be very bearish for the yellow metal.
A breach of US$352.50 on the upside would take gold bullion into the US$367 range. Bullion was not trading on Monday because of a market holiday in Britain.

"So you've got five points upside from here (to US$352.50 an ounce), and five points downside from here (to US$343 an ounce). We are sitting absolutely in very neutral zone -- it's like a mine field," Maison Placements technical analyst Joe Ismail said.

"The index was sloppy and it continued to drop down. The index, 9300 (is a good support level). I think when you break 9000, there's a major critical support zone on that index at 8750. If you take the 8750 on that group, forget it."
Ismail said the index is probably being kept from a rebound because of negative sentiment, which is chiefly a result of the Bre-X jitters.
((Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com))
